newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks pare losses at close.
newsitem.headline: French stocks pare losses at close.

text.p: The CAC-40 share index ended a touch weaker on Friday, retracing most of the day's losses, and clinging just below the key 2,900 level.
The market was consolidating after the week's run up, which saw record highs being reached. Brokers said there was potential for more gains, with non-domestic investors buying French stocks.
The CAC-40 index closed down 2.60 points or 0.09 percent at 2,891.04, but was up 4.86 percent from last week. The CAC-40 futures contract was down eight at 2,886 from Thursday's close.
Volume was a reasonably busy 10.99 billion francs.

L'Oreal saw heavy trading with 1.2 billion francs of volume. Two blocks of 195,000 shares changed hands at 2,510 and 2,511 francs per share. Traders said the business was probably tied to an upcoming dividend payment. The stock closed unchanged at 2,500.

Rhone-Poulenc also saw brisk business, with 2.8 million shares traded. Investors booked profits after Thursday's rise of nearly 20 percent, on the back of its buy-out offer for U.S. Rorer. The stock closed down 4.44 percent at 241.3.

LVMH bounced 2.59 percent to 1,547. It declined comment on a Guardian newspaper report it was in secret talks with Guinness and Grand Met to settle their row over the merger of the two British companies.
Canal Plus firms 4.63 percent to 1,130 francs, with the group repeating its forecast of nearing break-even this year after absorbing Nethold.
Pathe recovered from weakness earlier in the session, after a sharp fall in BSkyB, in which it holds a stake. The French media group closed up 0.86 percent at 1,170.
Usinor jumped 3.86 percent to 107.5 on the back of its entry to the CAC index on July 25.
Saint-Gobain closed down 0.12 percent at 856 francs. Merrill Lynch upgraded its recommendation to "buy" from "accumulate" and set a target price of 1,100 francs per share, market sources said.
Carrefour closed down 1.86 percent at 4,330, a prime candidate for profit-taking as the stock is viewed as expensive compared to other French retailers such as Casino and Promodes, a broker said.
Casino was off 0.03 percent at 299.9 and Promodes was down 3.2 percent at 2,329.
